title: Limited reserves and an inflationary gap: an open market operation, the money market, bonds and unemployment
scenario: The invented country of Calder is producing above full-employment output, and its price level is rising. Calder's central bank operates with limited reserves.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Identify the open market operation the central bank should use to close the gap.

rubric.point: States that the central bank sells government bonds (an open market sale)

parts.sample: The central bank should sell government bonds on the open market.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Draw a correctly labeled graph of the money market and show the effect of the open market operation you identified in part A on the nominal interest rate.

key.because: a central bank sale of bonds

slips.MD: A bond sale drains reserves and lowers the money supply; it does not change how much money people want at each rate.

rubric.point: A correctly labeled money market: nominal interest rate on the vertical axis, quantity of money on the horizontal axis, downward-sloping MD and vertical MS

accept: MS1 to MS2 to the left

rubric.point: A higher nominal interest rate shown on the vertical axis (i2 above i1)
accept: i rises from i1 to i2

parts.sample: Vertical axis: nominal interest rate (i). Horizontal axis: quantity of money. MD slopes down; the vertical MS1 crosses it at i1. The bond sale shifts the money supply left to MS2, which crosses MD at i2, above i1.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: What happens to the prices of existing bonds in Calder because of the open market operation? Explain.

rubric.point: States that bond prices fall, because the central bank's sales add to the supply of bonds (equivalently, because interest rates rise and bond prices move opposite to them)
accept: bond prices decrease as interest rates rise

parts.sample: Bond prices fall. The central bank's sales add bonds to the market, pushing their prices down; falling bond prices are the same thing as rising interest rates, since the two move in opposite directions.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Explain how the change in the nominal interest rate you showed in part B affects aggregate demand in Calder.

rubric.point: States that interest-sensitive spending (investment, or consumption of durable goods) decreases, because borrowing costs more
accept: investment falls because of higher interest rates

rubric.point: States that aggregate demand decreases (shifts left)

parts.sample: The higher interest rate raises the cost of borrowing, so firms invest less and households buy fewer cars and homes. Because investment and consumption are parts of aggregate demand, AD decreases (shifts left).

parts.label: E
parts.prompt: Based on your answer to part D, what happens to unemployment in Calder in the short run?

rubric.point: States that unemployment increases (consistent with a decrease in AD)

parts.sample: Unemployment increases: with lower aggregate demand, firms produce less real output and need fewer workers.

parts.label: F(i)
parts.prompt: The required reserve ratio in Calder is 0.1. Calculate the money multiplier. Show your work.

rubric.point: Money multiplier = 1 / 0.1 = 10, with the work shown

parts.label: F(ii)
parts.prompt: The central bank sells \$50 million of bonds to commercial banks. Calculate the maximum change in the money supply. Show your work.

rubric.point: A decrease of \$500 million: \$50 million x 10, with the direction (decrease) and the work shown

parts.sample: The banks pay with \$50 million of reserves and no deposits change, so excess reserves fall by \$50 million. Maximum change = \$50 million x 10 = \$500 million decrease in the money supply.
